rules.title: Security Deposit Law – maximum security deposit
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit. A pet security deposit may not be charged if, combined with the regular security deposit, it exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.key_value: 1.5 times one month's rent; yearly increase capped at 10% of current deposit
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. Landlords are not required to collect a deposit, but if they do they must follow the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant makes the law applicable to their tenancy 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord that the landlord fulfill the requirements of the Security Deposit Law.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

rules.title: No eviction solely because the lease term ended
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended; the only reason a landlord can terminate a lease is if the landlord offers a new lease with different terms and the tenant does not agree.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended.
